title: Sparc3D + Metahuman?
author: Accomplished-Exit708
selftext: Noob here. I want to create a realistic (making a game for Unreal Engine) character for my game with with a monkey like face & hair and a loincloth. Should I model the whole thing in Sparc3D or is there a way I can use metahuman (remember, monkey like face) directly. If I use Sparc3D, will I have to model the hair & cloth later in UE? Very confused!

comments.author: Aggressive_Finish798
comments.body: Produce a monkey face and body with the MetaHuman 5.6 creator as best you can. Export the new MetaHuman to Maya. Bring the face and body into Zbrush, but don't change the mesh topology. Can you achieve the loom you want using the original MetaHuman topology? If you think so, them proceed to modeling the highpoly face and body. Cloths are completely separate and get skinned and rigged like on any other character pipeline.

comments.author: MeowChat_im
comments.body: How is the topology of the mesh generated by Sparc3D?  MetaHuman expect certain topology in order to work. You would prob. need to retopologize the mesh generated by any 3D mesh generation models.

replies.author: Quind1
replies.body: How does this compare to CC4/CC5 or Daz?

replies.author: Quind1
replies.body: No. I tried it, and it is fairly limited in terms of clothing/gear options. You can't import your own outfits at this time, although it shows as being on their roadmap.  I would recommend Character Creator 4/5 over this at this time because you can import those straight to Unreal via the Unreal pipeline, which is free for indie devs: [https://www.reallusion.com/iclone/live-link/unreal-engine/indie.html](https://www.reallusion.com/iclone/live-link/unreal-engine/indie.html)
